# lane-routing

runIn lane-routing: r.job pinned to api/worker deploy-lanes, event-chain via ctx.events.append, verified end-to-end through createAllInOneEntrypoint.

## README

# Lane Routing

Pin jobs to deploy lanes (`api` | `worker`) with event-triggered fan-out.

## What it shows

- `r.job({ runIn: "worker" })` after an HTTP write
- `trigger: { maintenance: true }` for a daily housekeeping job in the app's maintenance window (`KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW`)
- `wakesSleepingApp: false` on a cron trigger for upkeep that must not wake a sleeping shared app
- End-to-end verification via `createAllInOneEntrypoint`

## Source

Feature entry point: `src/feature.ts`.

## Tests

Needs the Postgres from the repo root's `docker-compose.yml` (`docker compose up -d`); `TEST_DATABASE_URL` defaults to `postgresql://kumiko:kumiko@localhost:15432/kumiko_test`.

```bash
cd samples/recipes/lane-routing
bun test
```

### src/__tests__/feature.integration.test.ts

```ts
// Lane-Routing Sample — End-to-End Proof
//
// What we're proving (via createAllInOneEntrypoint + BullMQ + Hono — no
// framework-internal shortcuts):
//   1. A write lands on the HTTP surface.
//   2. The handler appends the "order-placed" event; the job-trigger event
//      consumer (auto-wired by the entrypoint) enqueues both jobs after the commit.
//   3. Both `runIn: "worker"` jobs fan out onto the `kumiko-jobs-worker`
//      queue and execute — the worker-side BullMQ worker picks them up,
//      the api-side one does not (even in all-in-one, the lane-scoped
//      dispatch() routes the job to the right queue).
//
// If the feature were wired with `runLocalJobs: true`-style api-lane
// jobs, the scaling.md pick-guide would apply — this sample stays
// worker-only because that's the prod default.

import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { createRegistry } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine";
import { createAllInOneEntrypoint } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/entrypoint";
import {
  createArchivedStreamsTable,
  createEventsTable,
} from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/event-store";
import { createEventConsumerStateTable } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/pipeline";
import { TestUsers } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/seeding";
import { waitFor } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers";
import {
  createTestDb,
  createTestRedis,
  pushEntityProjectionTables,
  type TestDb,
  type TestRedis,
} from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/stack";
import {
  createLaneRoutingFeature,
  pruneRuns,
  renderedReceipts,
  sentConfirmations,
} from "../feature";

const JWT = "lane-routing-sample-secret-minimum-32-chars!";
const adminUser = TestUsers.admin;

let testDb: TestDb;
let testRedis: TestRedis;

beforeAll(async () => {
  [testDb, testRedis] = await Promise.all([createTestDb(), createTestRedis()]);
  await createEventsTable(testDb.db);
  await createArchivedStreamsTable(testDb.db);
  await createEventConsumerStateTable(testDb.db);
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await Promise.all([testDb.cleanup(), testRedis.cleanup()]);
});

afterEach(() => {
  renderedReceipts.length = 0;
  sentConfirmations.length = 0;
  pruneRuns.length = 0;
});

describe("lane-routing sample", () => {
  test("order.create fans out to render-receipt + send-confirmation on the worker lane", async () => {
    const registry = createRegistry([createLaneRoutingFeature()]);
    await pushEntityProjectionTables(testDb, registry);
    const redisUrl = `redis://${testRedis.redis.options.host}:${testRedis.redis.options.port}/${testRedis.redis.options.db}`;
    const entry = createAllInOneEntrypoint({
      rowLevelSecurity: "off",
      registry,
      context: { db: testDb.db, redis: testRedis.redis },
      jwtSecret: JWT,
      redisUrl,
      queueNamePrefix: `lane-routing-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`,
    });
    await entry.start();
    try {
      const token = await entry.jwt.sign(adminUser);
      const res = await entry.app.request("/api/write", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          "Content-Type": "application/json",
          Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          type: "orders:write:order:create",
          payload: { customerName: "Acme GmbH", amount: 299 },
        }),
      });
      const result = (await res.json()) as { isSuccess: boolean; data: { id: string } };
      expect(result.isSuccess).toBe(true);
      const orderId = result.data.id;

      // Both jobs are declared runIn:"worker" — they enqueue into
      // kumiko-jobs-worker-*, and the all-in-one worker runner consumes
      // them. Without welle-2.6 the enqueue would drop silently (welle-2.5
      // gap) or the routing would hit the wrong queue.
      await waitFor(() => {
        expect(renderedReceipts).toHaveLength(1);
        expect(sentConfirmations).toHaveLength(1);
        expect(renderedReceipts[0]?.orderId).toBe(orderId);
        expect(sentConfirmations[0]?.amount).toBe(299);
      });
    } finally {
      await entry.stop();
    }
  });

  test("a maintenance job is registered for the daily window and runs on the worker lane", async () => {
    const registry = createRegistry([createLaneRoutingFeature()]);
    expect(registry.getJob("orders:job:prune-old-receipts")?.trigger).toEqual({
      maintenance: true,
    });
    expect(registry.getJob("orders:job:warm-receipt-cache")?.trigger).toEqual({
      cron: "*/15 * * * *",
      wakesSleepingApp: false,
    });
    const redisUrl = `redis://${testRedis.redis.options.host}:${testRedis.redis.options.port}/${testRedis.redis.options.db}`;
    const entry = createAllInOneEntrypoint({
      rowLevelSecurity: "off",
      registry,
      context: { db: testDb.db, redis: testRedis.redis },
      jwtSecret: JWT,
      redisUrl,
      queueNamePrefix: `lane-routing-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`,
      maintenanceWindow: { hour: 5, minute: 30 },
    });
    await entry.start();
    try {
      await entry.jobRunner.dispatch("orders:job:prune-old-receipts", {});
      await waitFor(() => expect(pruneRuns).toHaveLength(1));
    } finally {
      await entry.stop();
    }
  });
});
```

### src/feature.ts

```ts
// Lane-Routing Sample
//
// Shows `r.job({ runIn: "worker" })` end-to-end: an HTTP write emits an
// event, the event fans out to two worker-lane jobs via BullMQ, and the
// jobs actually execute on the worker lane (kumiko-jobs-worker queue).
//
// Deploy-shape: any of the three entrypoints. The test uses
// createAllInOneEntrypoint so the Single Integration-Test covers the full
// path without having to coordinate two processes.

import {
  createEntity,
  createNumberField,
  createTextField,
  defineFeature,
  emitEvent,
  type FeatureDefinition,
} from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine";
import { z } from "zod";

// In-memory collectors so the integration-test can assert both jobs ran
// and got the right payload. A real app would do DB writes, HTTP calls,
// PDF rendering, mail sending — whatever the side-effect is, it's
// opaque to the framework.
export const renderedReceipts: Array<{ orderId: string; amount: number }> = [];
export const sentConfirmations: Array<{ orderId: string; amount: number }> = [];
export const pruneRuns: number[] = [];

// The entity declaration secures the qualified-name prefix "orders:write:order:create"
// for the write handler below. The handler does not persist the entity — it
// appends the "order-placed" event the jobs trigger on; in a real app an
// entityWriteHandler would write to the DB.
const orderEntity = createEntity({
  name: "order",
  table: "read_orders",
  fields: {
    customerName: createTextField({ personal: { of: "id" }, find: "none", required: true }),
    amount: createNumberField({ required: true }),
  },
});

export function createLaneRoutingFeature(): FeatureDefinition {
  return defineFeature("orders", (r) => {
    r.entity(orderEntity);

    // The event both jobs trigger on. No PII: customerName stays out of it.
    const orderPlaced = r.defineEvent(
      "order-placed",
      z.object({ orderId: z.string(), amount: z.number() }),
      {
        piiFields: "none",
      },
    );

    // Write handler — runs in the API process (or wherever the command
    // lands) and appends the event the jobs consume.
    r.writeHandler({
      name: "order:create",
      schema: z.object({
        customerName: z.string().min(1),
        amount: z.number().positive(),
      }),
      handler: async (event, ctx) => {
        const orderId = crypto.randomUUID();
        await emitEvent(ctx, orderPlaced, {
          aggregateId: orderId,
          aggregateType: "order",
          payload: { orderId, amount: event.payload.amount },
          expectedVersion: 0,
        });
        return {
          isSuccess: true as const,
          data: {
            id: orderId,
            customerName: event.payload.customerName,
            amount: event.payload.amount,
          },
        };
      },
      access: {
        openToAll: {
          reason:
            "demo recipe: any signed-in user may place an order; the handler is a stub with no persistence",
        },
      },
    });

    // Receipt-rendering: heavy CPU work. Pinned to `worker` so the
    // BullMQ consumer on the API process never picks it up — even if the
    // API happens to run runLocalJobs for something else. `runIn` is the
    // Welle-2.6 contract that makes this stable across deploy shapes.
    r.job({
      name: "render-receipt",
      trigger: { on: "order-placed" },
      runIn: "worker",
      handler: async (payload) => {
        renderedReceipts.push({
          orderId: payload["orderId"] as string,
          amount: payload["amount"] as number,
        });
      },
    });

    // Confirmation-mail: external I/O. Also worker-lane. Both jobs fan
    // out from the same event in parallel — BullMQ handles their order
    // independently.
    r.job({
      name: "send-confirmation",
      trigger: { on: "order-placed" },
      runIn: "worker",
      handler: async (payload) => {
        sentConfirmations.push({
          orderId: payload["orderId"] as string,
          amount: payload["amount"] as number,
        });
      },
    });

    // Housekeeping: `maintenance` runs once a day in the app's maintenance window
    // (KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW, UTC, default 03:00) instead of a cron time of its own, so a
    // sleeping app wakes once a day for all its cleanup jobs.
    r.job({
      name: "prune-old-receipts",
      trigger: { maintenance: true },
      runIn: "worker",
      handler: async () => {
        pruneRuns.push(Date.now());
      },
    });

    // Optional upkeep: `wakesSleepingApp: false` keeps a sleeping shared app asleep when a run is
    // due; the run happens on the next wake instead.
    r.job({
      name: "warm-receipt-cache",
      trigger: { cron: "*/15 * * * *", wakesSleepingApp: false },
      runIn: "worker",
      handler: async () => {},
    });
  });
}
```
